verdict.rationale: OpenHands ships a documented HTTP/WebSocket Agent Server with an OpenAPI spec, and the SDK/API expose conversation control, goals, async execution, custom agents/tools, and automation hooks (openhands-docs-32, openhands-probe-2, openhands-docs-24, openhands-docs-25, openhands-docs-13). This shows deep, near-parity API access to core agent functionality, but there's no explicit vendor statement of full UI/API feature parity and some UI-specific elements (e.g., interactive CLI keybindings, browser session replay UI) aren't confirmed as fully API-drivable. Missing for 10: explicit parity statement, independent verification that every UI action maps to an API call, and coverage of CLI-only interactive controls via API.
